sentences.text: Palaeortyx was an extinct bird that ate seeds.
The genus Palaeortyx was described by Milne-Edwards in 1869.
Scientists have recorded 30 fossil occurrences of this bird in the Paleobiology Database.
The parent group of Palaeortyx is the family Phasianidae.
Palaeortyx is classified in the family Phasianidae.
Six species are recognized within the genus Palaeortyx, including P. caluxyensis, P. edwardsi, P. gallica, P. intermedia, P. major, and P. miocaena.
The time range for Palaeortyx is from the Rupelian to the Piacenzian, spanning 33.9 to 2.58 million years ago.
Fossils of Palaeortyx have been found in Germany, France, Italy, Hungary, and Romania.
It is debated whether Palaeortyx belongs to the family Phasianidae or Odontophoridae.
